group: PSI Score: Pneumonia Severity Index for CAP
question:
Patient note:
A 39-year-old woman who runs her own catering business and lives with her partner in a downtown loft walked into the emergency department late this morning complaining of two days of high-spiking fevers, shaking chills, and a cough that began as a dry tickle but overnight produced rust-colored sputum; she noted sharp right-sided chest discomfort whenever she drew a deep breath and became so short-winded climbing the single flight of stairs to her apartment that she had to stop twice, something she had never done before. Wanting the clinical staff to evaluate her “untouched,” she refused the antipyretic her partner offered at home, took no antibiotics or inhalers, and declined the pulse-dose corticosteroid prescription left over from an ankle sprain, then rode to the hospital in a rideshare with the windows cracked. Her past history is notable only for a small left parietal cortical ischemic event three years ago attributed to a patent foramen ovale that was subsequently closed percutaneously; she completed six months of dual antiplatelet therapy, has had no recurrent neurologic symptoms, and continues to work full-time without restrictions. She has never been told she has kidney trouble, chronic liver problems, cancer, or any condition that limited her activity. She quit smoking during college after a three-pack-year exposure, drinks wine only at family gatherings, and does not use illicit substances. Vaccination records in the state registry confirm receipt of both recommended pneumococcal formulations and this season’s inactivated influenza shot administered by an occupational health nurse two months ago. Her only routine medication is a combined ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel oral contraceptive, taken the previous evening with dinner. On presentation she was sitting upright on the stretcher, speaking coherently in full sentences, correctly identifying the date, location, and the current national holiday; pupils were equal and reactive, and a brief mini-mental test yielded a perfect score, indicating preserved cognition. Untreated vital signs at triage were: oral temperature 101.8 °F, a rapid and regular radial pulse of 140 beats per minute confirmed on telemetry as sinus tachycardia, automated right-arm blood pressure 149/83 mm Hg verified manually, respirations counted for a full minute at 59 breaths per minute with shallow excursions and visible accessory muscle use, and pulse oximetry on ambient air fluctuating between 95 % and 96 % at this sea-level facility. Capillary refill was brisk, but mucous membranes were visibly dry. Cardiac examination revealed a forceful precordial impulse with a crisp S1 and S2, no murmurs, gallops, or rubs. Pulmonary auscultation demonstrated markedly diminished breath sounds over the inferior half of the right posterior hemithorax with stony dull percussion and faint late-inspiratory crackles just superior to that zone; the left lung transmitted vesicular sounds throughout without wheezes. Abdomen was soft and non-tender; liver edge was not palpable, and no splenomegaly or shifting dullness was present. There was no peripheral edema or jugular venous distention. Neurologic screening showed intact cranial nerves, symmetric strength, steady finger-to-nose maneuver, and stable gait when she briefly stood at bedside. A bedside glucometer, applied before any intravenous line was flushed, read 131 mg/dL. Venous blood drawn within ten minutes of arrival, prior to any crystalloid bolus or medication, demonstrated sodium 164 mEq/L, potassium 4.0 mEq/L, chloride 118 mEq/L, bicarbonate 24 mEq/L, blood urea nitrogen 65 mg/dL, and creatinine 0.8 mg/dL. Complete blood count revealed leukocytes 15.6 × 10⁹/L with 87 % neutrophils, hematocrit 44 %, hemoglobin 14.9 g/dL, and platelets 265 × 10⁹/L. An arterial sample drawn from the right radial artery while she remained on room air returned a pH of 7.40, PaCO₂ 32 mm Hg, PaO₂ 103 mm Hg, and calculated bicarbonate 20 mEq/L, reflecting a modest respiratory alkalosis that balanced to an overall normal hydrogen ion concentration. Serum lactate measured 2.2 mmol/L. High-sensitivity troponin fell below the assay detection threshold. A portable postero-anterior chest radiograph obtained before any antibiotics or fluids demonstrated dense consolidation occupying the right middle and lower lobes with air bronchograms and a crescent-shaped opacity blunting the right costophrenic angle, compatible with a moderate fluid collection; the cardiac silhouette and mediastinum were unremarkable for age, and the left lung field was clear. Electrocardiography displayed sinus tachycardia at 138 bpm without acute ST-T changes. Two sets of peripheral blood cultures, an induced sputum specimen, urinary antigen assays for common bacterial pathogens, and a respiratory viral PCR panel were dispatched to the laboratory prior to the initiation of any antimicrobial or supportive therapy. Up to the instant this narrative is finalized she has received no intravenous fluids beyond minimal saline used to keep two small-bore catheters patent, no oxygen supplementation, no antipyretics, no bronchodilators, and no vasoactive agents, ensuring that every vital sign, laboratory value, and imaging finding above reflects her untreated physiologic state on arrival.

Question: What is the patient's Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
Apply the Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) to the untreated admission findings.
- Demographics: female age adjustment gives 39 − 10 = 29. She lives at home, so no nursing-home points.
- Comorbidities: prior ischemic stroke counts as cerebrovascular disease despite full recovery = 10. No heart failure, renal disease, liver disease, or malignancy = 0 each.
- Examination: respiratory rate 59/min (≥30) = 20; pulse 140/min (≥125) = 10. Mentation is normal = 0; systolic BP 149 mm Hg (not <90) = 0; temperature 101.8 °F, approximately 38.8 °C (neither <35 nor ≥40) = 0.
- Laboratory findings: BUN 65 mg/dL (≥30) = 20. Sodium 164 mEq/L earns 0 because only sodium <130 scores. Arterial pH 7.40 (not <7.35), glucose 131 mg/dL (not ≥250), hematocrit 44% (not <30%), and PaO₂ 103 mm Hg (not <60) = 0 each.
- Imaging: moderate right pleural effusion = 10.
Total = 29 + 10 + 20 + 10 + 20 + 10 = 99.
Final answer: 99
